skill.name: break-ui
skill.description: Stress-test UI components with realistic edge-case data, a development-only comparison toggle, and actionable reports covering layout, formatting, missing data, and collection states.
skill.summary: Expose UI failures with realistic worst-case fixtures and propose targeted fixes before changing the component.
skill.author: emilkowalski

content.user_title: Stress-Test UI With Realistic Edge Cases
content.value_statement: Demo data can hide layout failures, missing states, and incorrect formatting. This skill guides realistic fixture creation, development-only comparisons, and reports with targeted fixes.
actual_capabilities: Map rendered fields to data sources, types, optional values, and validation limits.
Build realistic fixtures covering long text, missing fields, Unicode names, extreme numbers, media failures, and collection states.
Add a development-only fixture toggle or a standalone HTML comparison.
Check layouts at real container widths, 320 pixels, wide layouts, and 200 percent zoom, with supported dark mode and RTL.
Report observed failures, likely causes, proposed fixes, design decisions, and cases that already work.
Apply requested fixes using project conventions and recheck both demo and worst-case states.
limitations: Visual verification requires browser tooling; otherwise, findings are inferred from CSS and must be identified as inferred.
This skill provides instructions and a test catalog, not a bundled test runner or automatic continuous integration setup.
It does not redesign components, critique visual taste, or review animation.
Fixtures depend on available project contracts and realistic assumptions when validation limits are absent.

use_cases.title: Check a Component Before Release
use_cases.description: Test member rows with long emails, short names, missing avatars, and mixed statuses before shipping.

use_cases.title: Compare Layout Decisions
use_cases.description: Use a fixture toggle to compare wrapping, truncation, empty states, and narrow layouts before approving design changes.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Data-Dependent Failures
use_cases.description: Create reusable fixtures for localization, collection boundaries, and missing data, then verify requested fixes across every state.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress-test [component] with realistic worst-case data. Add a development-only comparison toggle and report failures before applying fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Fixtures Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Data only [component]. Map its fields and limits, then create demo, worst-case, empty, and single-item fixtures with a development-only toggle.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare repeatable test data without a failure report.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Responsive and Localized States
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress-test [screen] at its real container width, 320 pixels, and its widest supported layout. Check 200 percent zoom and supported RTL and dark mode. Separate visually verified findings from inferred findings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: inspect a screen across layout and language conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Selected Fixes and Recheck
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix findings 1 and 3 from the previous report using existing project conventions. Recheck every fixture state and supported layout. Keep fixtures for regression checks and keep the toggle development-only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: resolve selected findings after reviewing the report.

output_examples.input: Stress-test a member list with long emails and missing avatars.
output: Illustrative finding: a long email pushes the action menu outside a narrow row, making the action unreachable.
Proposed fix: allow the text column to shrink and wrap while preserving the action width.
Design decision: wrap the full email or shorten it with access to the complete value.
What held up: the missing-avatar fallback retained its size in the tested state.

output_examples.input: Review counts and empty states in a dashboard.
output: Illustrative finding: a count of one displays a plural label.
Proposed fix: use locale-aware pluralization and verify zero, one, and larger counts.
Illustrative finding: zero items leaves a blank content region.
Design decision: choose an empty-state message and an appropriate next action.

output_examples.input: Create data only for a project card grid.
output: Fixture plan: spread long titles, missing images, duplicate names, and large counts across separate cards.
Comparison states: Demo, Worst case, Empty, One, and a realistic large collection.
Delivery: a development-only fixture switch, or a self-contained HTML comparison when no project exists.

best_practices: Use plausible examples or actual validation limits, and use reserved example domains for fixture emails and URLs.
Inject fixtures at the existing data boundary and keep the comparison toggle out of production.
Review proposed fixes first, then verify approved changes against both demo and worst-case states.
anti_patterns: Using arbitrary oversized strings instead of plausible values or schema-backed limits.
Editing markup or CSS to manufacture failures rather than changing the input data.
Stopping after long-text tests while ignoring empty lists, singular counts, missing media, and translated labels.

faq.question: What does this skill test?
faq.answer: It tests realistic data boundaries, layout behavior, formatting, optional fields, media fallbacks, collection states, and supported display environments.

faq.question: Does it fix problems automatically?
faq.answer: The default workflow reports first and stops. Explicit fix requests apply selected changes; ambiguous design decisions remain for the user.

faq.question: Does it require a running application?
faq.answer: A project can use a development-only switch or prototype route. A standalone component can use a self-contained HTML comparison.

faq.question: Can it work without browser tooling?
faq.answer: Yes, but it reasons from CSS rather than confirming screenshots. It must distinguish inferred findings from visually verified findings.

faq.question: Should the toggle remain in production?
faq.answer: No. Keep it development-only or inside a prototype route, and retain fixtures for future regression checks.

faq.question: Is this a complete security or accessibility audit?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on UI behavior under realistic data and environment stress, not comprehensive security testing or accessibility certification.
